justifications.chosen: Take yasmāt with hi causally: “for/since …,” governing the whole statement.

options_considered: take karmajam with the nearer buddhi-yuktāḥ
take karmajam as a separate substantive, “what is born of action”
take karmajam as an adjective of phalam despite separation
justifications.chosen: karmajam modifies phalam, not buddhi-yuktāḥ: “the fruit born from actions.”

evidence.quote: karmajaṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā iti vyavahitena sambandhaḥ |
evidence.translation: “The construction, despite separation, is: ‘having abandoned the action-born fruit.’”
“The action-born fruit, born from actions, is the obtaining of desirable and undesirable bodies.”

options_considered: the primary padagloss: equanimity-buddhi; with Śaṅkara’s broader contextual alternative as ultimate-reality-vision
justifications.chosen: buddhi-yuktāḥ means “endowed with the buddhi of equanimity,” not merely “intelligent.”

evidence.translation: “being buddhi-yukta means being endowed with the buddhi of sameness/equanimity.”

evidence.quote: athavā buddhi-yogād dhanaṃjaya ity ārabhya paramārtha-darśana-lakṣaṇaiva sarvataḥ saṃplutodaka-sthānīyā karma-yogaja-sattva-śuddha-janitā buddhir darśitā
evidence.translation: “Or, from ‘buddhi-yoga, O Dhanaṃjaya’ onward, the buddhi shown is characterized by vision of ultimate reality, born of purity of sattva produced by karma-yoga.”

justifications.decision: Compound relation and scope in janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ
options_considered: released from bonds caused by a particular birth
released only after death from future births
released, even while living, from bondage consisting in birth itself
justifications.chosen: janma-bandha is “the bondage that is birth”; vinirmuktāḥ means released from that bondage even while living.

evidence.quote: janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ janmaiva bandhaḥ janma-bandhaḥ tena vinirmuktāḥ jīvanta eva janma-bandhāt vinirmuktāḥ santaḥ
evidence.translation: “janma-bandha-vinirmuktaḥ: birth itself is bondage; from that they are released—released from birth-bondage while still living.”

options_considered: the affliction-free supreme station, i.e. liberation
justifications.chosen: padaṃ anāmayam is the affliction-free supreme station of Viṣṇu, called liberation (mokṣa).

evidence.quote: padaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇoḥ mokṣākhyaṃ gacchanti anāmayaṃ sarvopadrava-rahitam ity arthaḥ
evidence.translation: “They go to the supreme pada of Viṣṇu, called mokṣa; anāmaya means free from every affliction.”

translation: For the wise, endowed with the buddhi of equanimity, having abandoned the action-born fruit—the obtaining of desirable and undesirable bodies—are freed, even while living, from the bondage that is birth, and go to the affliction-free station (pada), the supreme station of Viṣṇu called liberation (mokṣa).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation could attach karmajam to the nearer buddhi-yuktāḥ and produce “action-born intelligence”; Śaṅkara explicitly connects karmajaṃ with phalaṃ despite the separation.
It could render buddhi-yuktāḥ as merely “intelligent” or “rational”; the bhāṣya makes it samatva-buddhi, the buddhi of equanimity.
It could take janma-bandha as a loose “bond of birth”; Śaṅkara specifies that birth itself is bondage and that the release is while living.
It could translate padaṃ anāmayam as a generic “disease-free place/step”; the bhāṣya identifies it as Viṣṇu’s supreme pada, called mokṣa, free from all afflictions.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segments compounded expressions into members (karma + ja, buddhi + yukta, janma + bandha + vinirmukta); here they are reported as single inflected compound stems, as required for word-level analysis of compounds.

ByT5 gives yuktāḥ and vinirmuktāḥ under verbal/participial roots yuj and vinirmuc; here the inflected items are analyzed as subanta participial adjectives with the whole compound stems buddhi-yukta and janma-bandha-vinirmukta.
The printed sandhi form buddhi-yuktā hi lacks the pausal visarga; the analysis records surface buddhi-yuktāḥ and surface_in_sandhi buddhi-yuktā.
